lyrics:
[Intro: dreamy flute-like synth, soft boom-bap beat, a hum]

[Verse 1: soft, floating, sweetly sung]
I'm doing great, I'm doing yoga
I told my therapist it's over
She said "journal," so I drew a map
Of your new place and a little trap

[Pre-Chorus: harmonies bloom, bass slides]
I'm so evolved, I'm so serene
I only think about it when I breathe

[Chorus: sweetest melody, gentle beat, stacked voices]
I might booby-trap your porch
Paint cans on a string
Marbles on the stairs
A feather and a spring
I'm so mature, I've grown so much
I'd never do a thing
But I might booby-trap your porch
It's healthier than texting you, I'm sure

[Verse 2: soft, a little wicked]
She seems nice, I checked her page
She likes hiking and she's half my age
I wish them well, I wish them rain
I wish their smoke alarm a low battery

[Pre-Chorus: harmonies bloom, bass slides]
I'm so evolved, I'm so serene
I only think about it when I breathe

[Chorus: sweetest melody, gentle beat, stacked voices]
I might booby-trap your porch
Paint cans on a string
Marbles on the stairs
A feather and a spring
I'm so mature, I've grown so much
I'd never do a thing
But I might booby-trap your porch
It's healthier than texting you, I'm sure

[Bridge: beat drops, voice alone with the flute synth]
I won't, I won't
I returned the string
I'm fine
I kept one marble

[Final Chorus: full, high ad-libs floating on top]
I might booby-trap your porch
Paint cans on a string
Marbles on the stairs
A feather and a spring
I'm so mature, I've grown so much
I'd never do a thing

[Outro: hum, flute synth, one marble rolling across a floor]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 89 BPM, 4/4, A-flat major. Dreamy, swaying and sweet. A lullaby with a raised eyebrow.

VOICE: Female soprano, soft, airy and floating, with a relaxed, slightly slurred R&B phrasing that slides between notes. She sings everything prettily, including the worst ideas. Stacked harmonies in the chorus and high, wordless ad-libs at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: A breathy, flute-like synth melody. A soft, dusty boom-bap drum beat. A warm, sliding bass. Mellow electric piano chords. Faint vinyl crackle. A plucked guitar in the second verse. Sound effect: a marble rolling.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the flute synth and beat. 0:11 Verse 1. 0:33 Pre-chorus. 0:44 Chorus 1. 1:11 Verse 2. 1:33 Pre-chorus. 1:44 Chorus 2. 2:11 Bridge, no beat, four short lines. 2:25 Final chorus, six lines with ad-libs. 2:45 Outro, a hum and a marble rolling across a wooden floor at 2:52.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2020s alternative R&B: soft, warm and hazy, drums gentle, voice close and layered.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first chorus line, sung as sweetly as a nursery rhyme.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The film reference is a 1990 family comedy that today's parents grew up on, and the revenge is slapstick. The bridge is the grown-up part: she returns the string and keeps one marble.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Fake serenity, mischief, restraint, one small exception.
